## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve had to deal with it for so long. Before you quit tomorrow, would you be willing to give yourself one night to breathe and think through your options? We could talk about what’s been happening, and maybe look at whether taking leave, setting boundaries, or finding another job first would make things easier. I’ll support you either way—I just don’t want you to feel forced into making a huge decision at your lowest point.

## 2

I understand why some images can seem easy to dismiss, especially when they come through agencies or media organizations you may not trust. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on space photographs alone. People have measured Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, observed ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, and used different star patterns and shadow lengths in different places for centuries. Modern satellite communication, GPS, weather forecasting, and independent space missions also rely on Earth being a globe. Those are many separate lines of evidence pointing to the same conclusion.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules in the air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from lots of parts of the sky.

At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before the sunlight reaches us, leaving more reds, oranges, and pinks. That is why the sky can look so colorful at those times.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像有人在黑暗中轻轻说话。街灯被雨幕晕开，昏黄的光落在湿漉漉的路面上，映出摇曳的树影。远处偶尔驶过一辆车，轮胎划开积水，转眼又消失在巷口。屋里很安静，只有钟表的滴答声和屋檐落水的回响。空气带着泥土和青草的气息，凉意从窗缝钻进来。这样的夜晚让人有些孤单，却也格外安心，仿佛世界暂时放慢了脚步，只剩雨声陪着人慢慢入睡。
